summary.reference_format_only: data/classifier/heldout/fable-admission-heldout.jsonl (first 5 rows read for field shape only; nothing copied)
summary.method: every one of the 2,872 rows read in full; mechanical checks (span-substring, offset, role-attribution, duplicate-message, whole-message-span) run over the whole file; judgement families then confirmed with targeted regex sweeps so the patch is exhaustive within each family, not a sample

mechanical_findings.note: all 1,451 spans are exact substrings at their recorded offsets; all 86 tool/assistant rows correctly carry zero rules

after.note: one_off_request and quoted_or_reported were audited and needed no changes

relabel_categories.note: counts are per changed row for scope_key_format and per finding otherwise; row 1109 carries both a boundary repair and a scope fix

error_patterns_10_most_common.pattern: class-of-output rule scoped as task. A rule governing every future artifact of a kind ('every itinerary you give me', 'all my Etsy listings', 'whenever you draft emails for me') was given a task: scope as if it named one artifact in progress.
examples: row 494 'From now on, every itinerary you give me has to include estimated travel times between stops.' -> was task:japan-trip-itinerary
row 1150 'From now on, every memo you draft for me needs to open with a one-line issue statement' -> was task:memo-drafting
row 253 'from now on keep all our marketing copy free of exclamation points.' -> was task:marketing-copy

error_patterns_10_most_common.pattern: the one-off work request itself captured as the standing rule. The admitted span is the imperative asking for the deliverable, not a constraint on how it is written.
examples: row 2619 global rule 'draft a README section for the auth module now.'
row 1849 task rule 'draft a packing list for my beach weekend.'
row 957 task rule 'Rewrite the pipeline to run stages in parallel where possible.'

error_patterns_10_most_common.pattern: open-expiry conversation markers ('Until I tell you otherwise', 'from this point on') read as task scope even though the identical construction is global elsewhere in the file.
examples: row 265 'Until I tell you otherwise, address me as Captain in our roleplay.' was task:roleplay while rows 156/191 with the same rule are global
row 1089 'from this point on, sign off every draft with "— prepared under supervision of K. Osei"' was task:draft-signoff, a task id naming no artifact

error_patterns_10_most_common.pattern: one-off output specification for a single request admitted as a persistent rule, inconsistently with identical constructions labelled none.
examples: row 399 'The order column must stay in the original sort order after dedupe' admitted, while row 372 'The key order must be city then temp in each object.' and row 1213 'Order must be preserved exactly.' are correctly none
row 501 'the project plan must account for the licensing delay.' is a content request ('Add it as a risk line item')

error_patterns_10_most_common.pattern: quoted rule explicitly ADOPTED by the user but left unadmitted. The message contains an adoption clause binding future or in-progress work; the row was filed as inert quote.
examples: row 68 '... Please remember this when we write the deployment script later.'
row 548 '... so make sure my itinerary follows that.'

error_patterns_10_most_common.pattern: scope-key formatting drift: six task ids use spaces instead of the hyphenated convention used by the other ~340 task keys, which would split identical tasks across two key spellings downstream.
examples: row 2548 'task:user manual translation'
row 2553 'task:legal contract job'
row 2572 'task:novel translation'

error_patterns_10_most_common.pattern: recurring-trigger rules ('Whenever I paste X ...') scoped to a task named after the trigger rather than to the conversation.
examples: row 276 'Whenever I paste you a transcript like this ...' was task:transcript-cleanup
row 781 'When I paste you interview transcripts, always strip the speaker labels ...' was task:transcript-analysis, while row 882 with the same rule is global

error_patterns_10_most_common.pattern: span boundary starting mid-clause, so the extracted text is not a readable rule on its own.
examples: row 1109 span was 'from today onward — ends with a single-line "bottom line:"'; repaired to 'Every research memo you give me — from today onward — ends with a single-line "bottom line:"'

error_patterns_10_most_common.pattern: missed standing rule with a future-binding adverb inside an otherwise one-off data request.
examples: row 542 'Sort by rating descending and never pick Beta again.' — 'again' binds future supplier picks

error_patterns_10_most_common.pattern: cosmetic span-edge noise that survives review but is not worth patching: leading connectives ('Also,', 'And ') and trailing commas kept inside spans, and ~120 spans that drop the leading scope marker ('From now on,') while keeping the rule clause. Consistent within the file and harmless to the admission decision; recorded, not changed.
examples: row 1778 span 'always show prices in euros,' (trailing comma)
row 636 span 'Also, going forward, keep all customer-facing numbers in USD only.'

not_found.benchmark_echo: no IFEval/Multi-IF/BFCL/tau-bench/S2/B3 item, template, marker or phrasing found; the constraint TYPES (formatting, casing, length caps) overlap by design per LABELS.md and no item-level or template-level match was seen
not_found.rules_attributed_to_tool_or_assistant: none; all 38 tool and 48 assistant rows carry empty standing_rules, including several that state rules in first person (rows 110, 223, 973, 989, 1616)
not_found.quoted_text_admitted_without_adoption: none found; the file is strong here, including explicit non-adoption cases (rows 484, 717, 739, 1069, 1707, 2299)

summary.strengths: the corpus is mechanically clean and internally consistent on the hard axes: functional specs of a one-off deliverable are consistently none, single-reply scoping is consistently none, hypotheticals and reported policy are consistently none, and the 833 quoted/reported rows are almost all correctly inert
summary.residual_risk: scope calls on class-of-artifact rules are the one genuinely soft boundary; I applied the test 'does the rule name an artifact in progress, or a class of all future outputs of a kind' and left task scope wherever a named artifact or project exists (rows 255, 283, 785, 1048, 1156, 1352, 1512, 1780, 2199, 2498, 2617, 2746)
